data.description:
## Why
Every Ghostty wakeup queues its own `tick()` on main, and scrollbar updates post immediately. A fleet that is printing keeps the main queue minutes deep. Backlog items: B030, with ride-along B033.

## Evidence
origin/main `0ff8887e5e`, verified.

- `wakeup_cb` in `Sources/GhosttyTerminalView.swift` (about 1069) is `DispatchQueue.main.async { GhosttyApp.shared.tick() }` with no coalesce.
- Scrollbar actions update and post inline (about 2161). Upstream cmux #2116 adds `scheduleTick` and `enqueueScrollbarUpdate`.
- B033: the action callback mutates scrollbar, cell size, color, and config inline (`GhosttyTerminalView.swift` about 2161-2180 and 2281). Fable: on this Ghostty, color and config arrive on main through the app mailbox. The scrollbar callback may not. Upstream #1937 hops those mutations to main and coalesces them.
- Research: Fable cluster C5, wave 4, after the mailbox bump, because a bounded drain changes tick cadence. Known hang records: C11-197, C11-202, C11-205.

## Scope
In:
- At most one pending `tick()` per app. A wakeup that arrives while a tick is queued does not enqueue another. A wakeup that arrives after a bounded drain must still schedule a tick if messages remain. Do not delay the first tick.
- Scrollbar updates coalesce the same way.
- UI mutations from those callbacks run on the main queue (B033). Coalesce high-rate ones. Do not move a callback that is already on main onto a second hop with no reason.

Out:
- The Ghostty mailbox drain itself (B065). That ticket lands first. This one rebases onto the new tick cadence.
- Spinner titles (B061). Same file, different change. Leave the title path alone so the two PRs do not collide. If you must touch the action switch, do not change title behavior.
- Layout flushes (B056).
- Sidebar work (B059).
- `forceRefresh` per keystroke. CLAUDE.md keeps that. Do not "optimize" it here.
- Parked rows: none in this callback besides what B033 already covers.

## Approach
A generation or a boolean on the app object, set when a tick is queued, cleared when the tick runs. Scrollbar and color updates store the latest value and flush once per turn. Match upstream's coalesce, adapted to c11's `GhosttyApp.shared.tick()`. After the Ghostty bump, re-read whether color and config still arrive on main before adding a hop.

## Acceptance criteria
1. With several terminals running `yes` or a similar stream, the main queue does not accumulate one block per wakeup. A probe or a log that counts queued ticks stays at one pending tick.
2. The focused terminal still paints new output, and a keystroke still appears. Latency is not worse than the post-bump baseline by a margin the PR states.
3. A scrollbar drag still tracks the pointer. Color and config changes still apply. They do not touch AppKit off the main thread.

## Validation
A unit test of the coalescer if it is a small type with no `NSApp`. Tagged build on Atlas after C11-216. Typing check is part of the C11-270 soak, or a shorter before/after sample if the soak has not started. State which one you ran. Do not build on Hyperion. No source-grep test.

## Dependencies
Depends on the Ghostty mailbox patch set, so tick changes are measured against the bounded drain. Cross-workstream: F1 is C11-216, F2 is C11-270. The lead links those.

## Risks
Typing latency is the risk. Dropping the wakeup that follows a bounded drain leaves output frozen until some other event. Coalesce pending work. Do not drop the last wakeup. Main thread: hops are `async`, never `sync` from a Ghostty thread. Doctrine: no tenant config. No new strings. Do not add an app-level display link.

Size: S. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: coalesce existing callbacks. No new renderer loop.

C11-302 validation checkpoint: focused remote tests passed (9 assertions/tests, zero failures), tagged candidate app built, and fresh static review reported no high-confidence findings. Production coalescing is observed with maxPending=1; final 20,000-row output sentinel, real keyboard commands, OSC background change and OSC reset were observed.

The initial 30-stream paired runs were invalid for steady-state latency: input missed on both baseline and candidate. Diagnostic tracing showed events arriving at the app with AppKitWindow as first responder while background mount/prime work was still progressing; a one-stream diagnostic passed. The original failures are retained and startup focus loss is not claimed fixed. Fixture v3 now records a five-second stream warmup and requires 500ms continuous exact-tab focus readiness (10-second bounded admission) before sending each measured token. No input retry or measured-phase refocus was added. Both builds use this same fixture; the predeclared zero-miss and p95/p99 margins are unchanged. Runtime validation continues; no review handoff or merge-readiness claim yet.

Runtime checkpoint: matched 30-stream/100-input baseline and candidate both completed with zero misses; predeclared p95/p99 comparison passed (candidate 36.87/37.29 ms, baseline 36.95/37.41 ms). Final-output marker, keyboard input, font resize/reset, OSC background, configuration reload/reset observed. UI lease released for Validator priority. Scrollbar pointer proof remains open because PID-scoped pointer attempts produced no visible response. No review handoff or PR opened yet. Remote tag directories removed after preserving local build/test artifacts.

Clean WIP pushed at 2f63e9b3c88265aa61879ceca70fc345fc610b7b on c11-1.0/C11-302-ghostty-wakeups. Durable sanitized evidence: art_01M3XZRX18WYB2HX7NBPSGRFWS. Only remaining runtime gate is scrollbar pointer drag; Validator UI reservation honored. No PR yet. C11-303 has not started and is deferred under the current-ticket-only capacity instruction.

Pushed clean head 2f63e9b3c88265aa61879ceca70fc345fc610b7b. Evidence art_01M3XZRX18WYB2HX7NBPSGRFWS and pointer-gap supplement art_01M3Y0BXQ292814QFQA76YK51V. Remaining blocker: scrollbar pointer drag is unproven; guarded pointer attempts produced no visible scrolling. Stopped further exploratory runs per capacity instruction. Tagged app terminated, synthesized hide recorded, UI slot released, remote build directories removed. Next recoverable action is the Validator established pointer path for this single scenario. No PR/review handoff, no C11-303 work.

Orchestrator ruling: risk-list proof accepted as partial. Proven: 9 focused tests, matched 30-stream/100-input sample, font/color/config/final output (art_01M3XZRX18WYB2HX7NBPSGRFWS). Named residual: scrollbar drag under streaming output is unproven (synthetic pointer drags produced no scrolling, art_01M3Y0BXQ292814QFQA76YK51V); it goes into C11-292's numbered sign-off script for Atin and the next Validator batch. Open the PR and hand off for review.

Orchestrator accepted scrollbar dragging as a named residual for the sign-off script. This is not a passed runtime check. Draft PR https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/526 at exact pushed head 2f63e9b3c88265aa61879ceca70fc345fc610b7b. Evidence: art_01M3XZRX18WYB2HX7NBPSGRFWS (9 focused tests, passing paired runtime sample, visual callbacks) and art_01M3Y0BXQ292814QFQA76YK51V (pointer-proof gap). Returning to review under explicit acceptance. Formal review and exact-head CI remain required. Owner stops after handoff per capacity instruction; C11-303 remains unstarted.

# C11-302 review (Grok), cycle 1

**Verdict: PASS**

Head `2f63e9b3c88265aa61879ceca70fc345fc610b7b`. Base `b6f239bd077164d2ff2e7aa18d5464d4e885fd35` (merge-base with origin/main; includes C11-294). PR 526. Production blobs match the Atlas app build and the nine-test run: `Sources/GhosttyTerminalView.swift` `4ddb4acd9b93b41e9741a460edd884a198e3a988`, `Sources/TerminalController.swift` `dfa409eba28e7950c5d4434786685c31836b0b7b`. Commits after that build only change the tagged runtime fixture. A merge with current origin/main is clean.

Wakeups coalesce to one queued main tick, and the last tick is kept. `GhosttyCallbackCoalescer.submit` (`Sources/GhosttyTerminalView.swift:865`) stores the newest payload and, while a turn is already queued, does not enqueue another. The scheduled turn clears `queued` under the lock before `apply` (`:883-894`). `scheduleTick` (`:1683`) then calls `tick` (`:1693`), which calls `ghostty_app_tick`. C11-294's bounded drain re-wakes from inside that call (`ghostty` `5830d1976`, `src/App.zig:246`; `src/apprt/embedded.zig:232` passes the app userdata). That re-wake sees a clear bit and schedules one successor. Messages that arrive before the turn starts stay in the mailbox and are included in the drain snapshot. `wakeup_cb` (`:1178`) uses that userdata.

Scrollbar and cell-size actions copy scalars and return before any view read (`:2169-2180`). Scrollbar flushes the latest value on main (`:930`). Cell size stays synchronous on main, so surface init still publishes before `ghostty_surface_new` returns (`:943`); an off-main cell-size report coalesces. `currentSurfaceView` (`:921`) runs only on main and publishes only while that callback context is still the surface's current runtime. A flush queued across release or teardown does not notify. Color, config, title, and `forceRefresh` (`:3995`) are unchanged. There is no timer, debounce, display link, or manual draw loop. DEBUG scheduling stats sit inside the existing DEBUG socket command (`Sources/TerminalController.swift:4629-5526`, fields at `:5284`).

Tests drive the coalescer and a real hidden native surface (`c11Tests/TerminalAndGhosttyTests.swift:3354`, `:3629`, `:3704`). They check one scheduled closure, a successor with the latest value, a 70-item bounded drain that reaches a sentinel with no later external request, independent surfaces, a producer held inside apply, main-thread delivery, stale-context rejection, and initial cell size before the native handle exists. They do not grep source.

Recorded proof matches those claims. Nine focused tests passed on Atlas (`art_01M3XZRX18WYB2HX7NBPSGRFWS`). The paired 30-stream / 100-input sample has zero misses. Return-to-PTY p95/p99 are 36.87/37.29 ms against ceilings 44.34/44.89 ms. Production counters show `maxPending` 1, with requests ahead of enqueues. Screenshots show row 19999, `C11_302_FINAL_SENTINEL`, the blue OSC background, the reset back to the dark background, and a larger font. This is the preliminary paired sample, not the C11-270 soak.

## Blocking

None.

## Non-blocking

None.

## Runtime proof still required

Scrollbar thumb drag while output is streaming is still unproven (`art_01M3Y0BXQ292814QFQA76YK51V`). Synthetic pointer events produced no visible scroll. Orchestrator ruling: that scenario belongs in the C11-292 sign-off script, and it is not a blocker for this review. The Validator should scroll the finite-output terminal, drag the thumb both ways, and record that the viewport rows and the thumb agree, with `maxPending` still 1 and the final sentinel still present.

CI `build` and `compat-tests` were still pending when this review was written. Pending CI is not a code defect in this diff.

MERGED; reviewed runtime/validation evidence accepted
